data.narrative:
Aleph Surgical is a seed-stage biotech company founded by Dylan and Ryan McGuire, valued within a comp universe of 3 public players (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers in the Biotech & Health sector. The company has raised $175K to date.

Only one valuation method proved applicable. Stage-Progression triangulation applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement to the $175K total raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $438K. Peer-Median analysis was not feasible: while 7 same-sector peers exist in the comp universe, none satisfied narrow filters requiring same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with sufficient sample size (minimum 3 datapoints). Public-Comp Anchoring could not be deployed due to lack of revenue disclosure—standard for private companies—which prevents application of the 7.4x sector P/S median observed across the three public biotech tickers.

The triangulated range is $372K to $503K (median $438K), supported entirely by stage-progression logic. Key uncertainties stem from the single-method result: the absence of private peer valuations and the target's undisclosed financial metrics limit confidence in this estimate. Conviction would increase materially with comparable seed-stage biotech transaction data or revenue guidance from the target.
